factProposals.value: Locate tickets are received from the one-call centre (Blue Stakes of Utah) and the city's response is sent back through a client with timeout, capped retries and a log row per attempt. Built against a stand-in feed and a stand-in centre.
A locate ticket moves received → in_progress → responded → completed; it can be answered more than once (e.g. needs more time, then marked) before completion.
A locate ticket cannot be completed until a final response has been delivered to the one-call centre; completed tickets cannot be changed or answered again.
locate_tickets, bluestakes_outbox and bluestakes_log tables exist; a locate ticket can be linked to a work order.

Changing locate tickets through the API needs the locate_tickets:write scope; no key gives 401, a key without the scope gives 403, and every refusal is audited. Changes record the person and the calling system.
Two new actors appear in the audit trail: 'bluestakes-feed' for imported tickets, and locators acting through an API client, recorded as '<person> via <system>'.

Blue Stakes of Utah's real ticket feed format, delivery method, official response codes and credentials are not known; the stand-in format and the codes marked, clear_no_conflict and needs_more_time are assumptions.

The STORY-013 brief says to use the existing Bluestakes data schema, that STORY-012 precedes it, and that it is the last story in the plan; no schema existed (it was built from the proposed locate_ticket table), STORY-012 is not built, and nine stories remain in Releases 1–4.

decisions.statement: Require a delivered, final response before a locate ticket can be completed.
decisions.rationale: A ticket must never be closed without the one-call centre being told the locate is done.

decisions.statement: Queue responses in an outbox in the same transaction as the response, then deliver with retries.
decisions.rationale: A one-call centre outage must not lose a response, and a resend must not deliver it twice (response_id).

decisions.statement: Reuse the STORY-011 API keys with a separate write scope instead of building user logins now.
decisions.rationale: Per-person access control belongs to STORY-007; a scoped key keeps read-only clients like Madison AI out of ticket changes today.

decisions.statement: Keep the response codes in one placeholder list.
decisions.rationale: The official codes are unknown; replacing the list is the only change needed once they are.

limitations.statement: The person acting is whatever name the calling system sends; there is no per-person login yet.
Re-sent tickets with changed details (amendments) are treated as duplicates and ignored.
Undelivered responses are resent only when deliverPendingResponses() is called; nothing runs it on a schedule.
Tickets arrive only through importLocateTicket(); there is no live feed connection or intake endpoint yet.
Due times are stored but not enforced: nothing warns when a ticket is close to or past due.
